title: An Autumn Flowering (Symphony)
program_note:
The first movement of An Autumn Flowering was begun in October, 1992, was completed in January, 1993, and was revised in December, 1993. The second and third movements were written between September and December, 1993, with revisions in March and April, 1994, and proofreading corrections made in October. The first and third movements are intended to be detachable pieces, performable individually.

One conceptual link between all of the movements are the titles suggestive of three seasons: An Autumn Flowering; Winterscape; and Coiled Spring. Of those titles, however, only the second is meant to be at all programmatic; there is a certain sense of stillness and frozen desolation in the music. The title of the first movement reflects the fact that the form somewhat parallels that of a Swedish Ivy flower that began blooming in my studio as I began the piece: as one set of three to five small flowers reaches maturity and then drop off, another set has already begun. Similarly in my music, as one phrase or group of phrases climaxes, another group has already begun. The title of the third movement relates to the pent-up energy that “springs” forth fairly frequently in the first portion of the work, and animates the remainder of the movement. The second movement moves attacca into the third movement.

The total duration of the work is approximately 18:45; the duration of the individual movements are approximately 9:00, 3:30, and 6:15.
